title: The families
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, vintage Christmas in an old house, glowing tree lights and hand-blown glass ornaments, deep red and gold tones with cold blue shadows, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 3. Eleven ornaments. Eleven families gone on Christmas Eve. 🕯️

Original fiction. Part 4 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: the twelfth ornament showed Holly's own living room, with a tiny Holly inside it.
scenes.image: a glowing glass ornament showing a miniature living room, held in a woman's palm

scenes.narration: Her front door was shut and locked. She checked it four times. Then she sat up all night at the kitchen table, the eleven ornaments lined up in a row.
scenes.image: woman at a kitchen table at night lit by a laptop, eleven glass ornaments lined up in front of her

scenes.narration: She started with the piano room. She searched old newspaper archives. Family. Missing. Christmas.
scenes.image: woman leaning close to a laptop glow in a dark kitchen, glass ornament beside the keyboard

scenes.narration: She found them. The Vogels, 1958. A farmhouse parlor with an upright piano. Gone on Christmas Eve. Tree lit. Dinner still warm on the table.
scenes.image: old black and white photograph of an empty 1950s farmhouse parlor with an upright piano and a lit Christmas tree

scenes.narration: The dog by the fire: the Ashworths, 1971. The green sofa: the Delaneys, 1983. On and on.
scenes.image: faded 1970s color photograph of an empty living room with a green sofa and a decorated tree

scenes.narration: Eleven ornaments. Eleven families. Every one gone on Christmas Eve. Every last photo taken in front of a tree with one clear glass ornament.
scenes.image: faded vintage photograph of two adults posing beside a Christmas tree, a single clear glass ornament glowing on a branch

scenes.narration: They weren't decorations. They were somebody's last Christmas, kept under glass.
scenes.image: close-up of a glass ornament catching candlelight, a tiny frozen room inside

scenes.narration: Holly called the nephew. He answered on the first ring, like he'd been waiting. She asked who the twelfth was for.
scenes.image: woman holding a phone to her ear in a dark kitchen, her face pale

scenes.narration: He was quiet a long time. Then he said: my aunt hung eleven to keep it hungry. The twelfth is for whoever owns the box.
scenes.image: the antique velvet box sitting alone on a kitchen counter, the twelfth slot faintly glowing

scenes.narration: And Holly, he said. It doesn't need you to hang it. It only needs you to fall asleep.
scenes.image: a woman's heavy-lidded eyes in dim light, a glowing ornament reflected in them
